entities.summary: Albert Gleizes was a French artist, theoretician, philosopher, a self-proclaimed founder of Cubism and an influence on the School of Paris. Albert Gleizes and Jean Metzinger wrote the first major treatise on Cubism, Du "Cubisme", 1912. Gleizes was a founding member of the Section d'Or group of artists. He was also a member of Der Sturm, and his many theoretical writings were originally most appreciated in Germany, where especially at the Bauhaus his ideas were given thoughtful consideration. Gleizes spent four crucial years in New York, and played an important role in making America aware of modern art.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gleizes' ideas on Cubism influenced a generation of artists and shaped the development of modern art in Europe and America. His writings were widely read and studied at the Bauhaus, contributing to the spread of modernist thought.
